incidente.resumo: On 21 April 2020 the Flowdock application database hung due to high CPU usage from a sudden surge in user activity, potentially linked to more users working remotely; after a restart, a corrupted user ID sequence table caused recently generated user IDs to be assigned to users of other organizations, exposing cross-organization flows. The application was unavailable for about 22 hours; service was restored by restoring a pre-crash database snapshot twice, invalidating all sessions and verifying, which lost user activity from the incident window.

observacoes: The overview gives a major incident of about 32 hours (written as April 21, 1:30 UTC to April 22, 21:30 UTC, while the timeline starts at ~13:30 UTC) and an unavailability of about 22 hours; the duration uses the stated unavailability. The document title says 22nd & 23rd April 2020, but the body dates the events April 21-22. Restoring the snapshot lost user activity from the incident window (new flows, new or updated users, users added to flows, failed Rally integration calls that removed integrations). The authors state the affected user IDs suggest very limited exposure of 1-1 conversations and that no .doc, .xls, .pdf or .csv files were downloaded. Page footers (copyright notice, page numbers) are included in the extracted text.
